stem: What role do the GameXPeptides studied here play for the entomopathogenic bacteria that make them?
choices: They suppress competing bacteria in the gut
They kill the bacteria's insect prey
They signal between bacteria and their nematode hosts
They protect the bacteria against insect antimicrobials
answer: They kill the bacteria's insect prey
label: Abstract · what GXP are for

stem: Why are conventional codon-based tests for natural selection unsuitable for non-ribosomal peptide synthetases?
choices: Their genes are too long for alignment-based statistics
They are horizontally transferred too often to carry a species signal
Their diversity comes from recombining large DNA stretches, not individual codon changes
Their products are peptides rather than folded proteins
answer: Their diversity comes from recombining large DNA stretches, not individual codon changes
label: Introduction · why new methods

stem: What happens to a phylogeny inferred from a single alignment of a recombination-rich NRPS gene?
choices: It reflects the history of the longest unrecombined stretch
It reflects the species history rather than the gene's
It reflects the history of the most recent recombinant segment
It may reflect the history of no part of the gene
answer: It may reflect the history of no part of the gene
label: Introduction · conflicting histories

stem: On what basis have families of non-ribosomal peptides historically been defined?
choices: Structural similarity of the peptides
Common descent of their synthetases
Shared host bacterial genus
Shared biological activity against a target
answer: Structural similarity of the peptides
label: Introduction · how NRP families are defined

stem: To about how many cells do the few colonizing Xenorhabdus or Photorhabdus grow inside a nematode, the bottleneck expected to cause drift in GXP structure?
choices: Around 10,000 cells
Around 100 cells
Around 10 cells
Around 1 million cells
answer: Around 100 cells
label: Introduction · population bottleneck

stem: Why did the authors choose the thioesterase domain as the phylogenetic yardstick for GxpS orthology?
choices: It is the fastest-evolving domain, giving the most resolution
It is the only domain shared with the outgroup NRPS KolS
It occurs once per synthetase and showed no detectable recombination
It carries the specificity-encoding sites that define the product
answer: It occurs once per synthetase and showed no detectable recombination
label: Results · TE-domain as yardstick

stem: How many putative GxpS orthologues went into the reference TTE-domain phylogeny?
label: Results · size of the reference tree

stem: Why did the authors add the thiolation domain to the thioesterase domain for the reference phylogeny?
choices: More sequence information and better congruence with the species and domain trees
It is the domain least affected by horizontal gene transfer
It carries the stereochemistry signal that distinguishes GxpS
It allowed rooting the tree with the related synthetase KolS
answer: More sequence information and better congruence with the species and domain trees
label: Results · why TTE rather than TE

stem: What origin and transfer history for GxpS did reconciling the gene tree with the species tree indicate?
choices: It arose in Xenorhabdus and was transferred to Photorhabdus twice
It arose in Photorhabdus and was transferred to Xenorhabdus twice
It arose in the common ancestor of both genera with no transfers
It arose in Photorhabdus and was transferred to Xenorhabdus once
answer: It arose in Photorhabdus and was transferred to Xenorhabdus twice
label: Results · origin of GxpS

stem: What history did the PAPA operon, whose product the A3 domain can incorporate, have in Xenorhabdus?
choices: Gained twice independently from Photorhabdus donors
Retained throughout, with loss only in Photorhabdus
Lost twice, then reacquired in X. doucetiae by horizontal transfer
Lost once and never regained in any Xenorhabdus
answer: Lost twice, then reacquired in X. doucetiae by horizontal transfer
label: Results · PAPA operon history

stem: In the A-domain tree, the A3 domain of the GxpS of Xenorhabdus sp. PB62.4 grouped with which sequence?
choices: The A3 domains of other GxpS orthologues
The A5 domains of other GxpS orthologues
The A2 domains of Photorhabdus asymbiotica
Its own A2 domain
answer: Its own A2 domain
label: Results · A2 overwrites A3

stem: How many A-domain recombinations did the initial congruence analysis of GxpS find in total?
label: Results · A-domain recombination count

stem: What did a multitree mixture model applied to an A3 and A5 domain alignment reveal about that alignment?
choices: A single history congruent with the TTE-domain tree
At least two distinct phylogenetic histories within it
A single history congruent with the species tree
Three histories, one per recombination breakpoint
answer: At least two distinct phylogenetic histories within it
label: Results · two histories in one alignment

stem: How many additional product-altering recombinations did iteratively disentangling the A3 clade uncover?
choices: Seventeen
Twelve
Five
Twenty-seven
answer: Five
label: Results · extra recombinations in A3

stem: How did the four-modular Xenotetrapeptide synthetase arise from a five-modular GxpS?
choices: A dual condensation/epimerization domain was replaced, truncating the product
A whole module was duplicated and then deleted by slipped-strand mispairing
A TCA-tridomain was excised without any foreign sequence
A foreign NRPS A-domain recombined with flanking regions, excising A4TC4A5
answer: A foreign NRPS A-domain recombined with flanking regions, excising A4TC4A5
label: Results · origin of XtpS

stem: Which combination of events produced the six-modular Gamehexpeptide synthetase?
choices: A TCA deletion plus an ATC duplication and an ATC insertion
A single ATC duplication with no deletions
Two successive ATC insertions from a foreign NRPS
A TCA excision followed by a whole-gene duplication
answer: A TCA deletion plus an ATC duplication and an ATC insertion
label: Results · origin of HexS

stem: How many GxpS variants with a product spectrum different from the canonical orthologue did the phylogenetic analysis identify?
choices: Twelve
Ten
Forty-nine
Fifty-four
answer: Ten
label: Results · variant count

stem: How many compounds, side products included, were detected across the isotope-feeding and co-injection experiments?
label: Results · compounds detected

stem: What did PAPA and mPAPA feeding experiments show about the phenylalanine-incorporating synthetases?
choices: Only the Photorhabdus synthetases could incorporate them
Only synthetases whose genome carries the PAPA operon could incorporate them
None could incorporate the methylated derivative mPAPA
All of them could incorporate PAPA and mPAPA as well
answer: All of them could incorporate PAPA and mPAPA as well
label: Results · PAPA promiscuity

stem: In Xenorhabdus species lacking the PAPA operon but keeping a phenylalanine-incorporating A3 domain, which peptide is the main product?
choices: GXPA
The mPAPA-containing peptide
A cyclic tetrapeptide
The valine-rich variant
answer: GXPA
label: Results · product without the operon

stem: Which experimentally determined products defied the phylogenetic predictions for GxpS orthologues?
choices: Linear pentapeptides from five-modular synthetases
Cyclic tetrapeptides from five-modular synthetases
Cyclic hexapeptides from five-modular synthetases
Cyclic pentapeptides from four-modular synthetases
answer: Cyclic tetrapeptides from five-modular synthetases
label: Results · unexpected tetrapeptides

stem: What was the outcome of disabling both the fifth thiolation domain and the thioesterase domain in a tetrapeptide-producing five-modular synthetase?
choices: Production stopped entirely
Only linear tetrapeptides were produced
Cyclic tetrapeptides were still produced
Cyclic pentapeptides were produced instead
answer: Cyclic tetrapeptides were still produced
label: Results · TE not needed for cyclization

stem: What did swapping the recombined C4 domain for the same synthetase's LCL-C2 domain produce?
choices: Only cyclic tetrapeptides
A mixture of cyclic tetra- and pentapeptides
Only linear pentapeptides
Only cyclic pentapeptides
answer: Only cyclic pentapeptides
label: Results · C4 swap

stem: Which peptide did the resurrected last common ancestor of all GxpS make as its main product?
choices: A cyclic pentapeptide with phenylalanine at position three
A cyclic tetrapeptide with leucine at position three
A cyclic pentapeptide with valine at positions two and four
A linear pentapeptide with leucine at position three
answer: A cyclic pentapeptide with phenylalanine at position three
label: Results · ancestral product

stem: At how many amino acid positions did the deliberately less likely alternative ancestral reconstruction differ from the main one?
label: Results · robustness of reconstruction

stem: How many times was the ancestral phenylalanine at position three independently replaced by leucine through A3-domain recombination?
choices: Twelve
Five
Seven
Two
answer: Seven
label: Results · convergent Phe to Leu

stem: How many convergent origins did the valine-rich GameXPeptide 4 have on the GxpS tree?
choices: Twelve
Seven
Two
Five
answer: Five
label: Results · convergent origins of peptide 4

stem: How often did four-modular GxpS synthetases arise on the tree?
choices: Twice, independently
Once, early in Photorhabdus
Three times, independently
Once in each bacterial genus, from a shared recombination
answer: Twice, independently
label: Results · convergent tetrapeptide producers

stem: How did the counts of synonymous and non-synonymous recombination events in GxpS compare?
choices: 26 synonymous against 27 non-synonymous
27 synonymous against 26 non-synonymous
27 synonymous against 5 non-synonymous
17 synonymous against 26 non-synonymous
answer: 27 synonymous against 26 non-synonymous
label: Results · synonymous vs non-synonymous

stem: What makes homotypic recombinations, between A-domains of the same substrate specificity, usable as a proxy for the neutral process?
choices: They are far more frequent than heterotypic recombinations
They occur only between domains of different genes
They leave the peptide structure unchanged, so selection is largely blind to them
They are too short to cover the specificity-encoding sites
answer: They leave the peptide structure unchanged, so selection is largely blind to them
label: Results · homotypic as neutral proxy

stem: How did the lengths of homotypic and heterotypic recombinations in GxpS compare?
choices: Heterotypic were mostly very short; homotypic were longer, up to whole modules
Both were short, differing only in where they fell
Both spanned whole domains, differing only in frequency
Homotypic were mostly very short; heterotypic were longer, up to whole modules
answer: Homotypic were mostly very short; heterotypic were longer, up to whole modules
label: Results · recombination lengths

stem: Where along the CAT-tridomain were homotypic recombination breakpoints most frequent?
choices: In the middle of the A-domain and the middle of the C-domain
In the CA-linker and at the end of the A-domain
At both ends of the C-domain only
Uniformly, with no positional preference
answer: In the middle of the A-domain and the middle of the C-domain
label: Results · breakpoint positions

stem: Relative to the homotypic neutral proxy, how often did heterotypic recombinations cover the A-domain specificity pocket?
choices: Much less often, a significant deficit
Much more often, a significant excess
About equally often, with no significant difference
More often, but not significantly so
answer: Much more often, a significant excess
label: Results · specificity-pocket excess

stem: Which model of insecticidal activity did the Akaike information criterion select across the eight peptides and four insect species?
choices: The one giving every peptide a single activity across insects
The one giving every insect a single susceptibility across peptides
The one giving every peptide-insect pair its own activity
The one with a shared activity for all pairs
answer: The one giving every peptide-insect pair its own activity
label: Results · peptide-insect specificity

stem: How did the peptide that was most active against Spodoptera exigua perform against Plutella xylostella?
choices: It was also the most effective
It was intermediate among the peptides tested
It was the only peptide with no measurable effect
It was among the least effective
answer: It was among the least effective
label: Results · activity crossover

stem: Which two of the four insect species tested were overall less susceptible to the GameXPeptides?
choices: Tenebrio molitor and Frankliniella occidentalis
Spodoptera exigua and Plutella xylostella
Spodoptera exigua and Tenebrio molitor
Plutella xylostella and Frankliniella occidentalis
answer: Tenebrio molitor and Frankliniella occidentalis
label: Results · less susceptible insects

stem: What feature of the insecticidal assay results leaves room for drift through chemically different peptides?
choices: One peptide dominated against every insect
Several peptides had similar potency against each insect
No peptide had measurable activity against any insect
Potency tracked the number of modules in the synthetase
answer: Several peptides had similar potency against each insect
label: Results · room for drift

stem: How did the sequence identity of the real A-domain recombination donors compare with same-specificity A-domains from other nrpS genes in the genome?
choices: The real donors were significantly less similar to the recipient
The two groups were equally similar to the recipient
The real donors were significantly more similar to the recipient
The real donors were more similar only for heterotypic events
answer: The real donors were significantly more similar to the recipient
label: Results · recombination bias

stem: Where did donor and recipient sit for most of the recombinations in the GxpS dataset?
choices: Both in other nrpS genes of the same genome
The donor in another nrpS gene and the recipient in gxpS
The donor in another bacterial genome via horizontal transfer
Both within the gxpS gene itself
answer: Both within the gxpS gene itself
label: Results · donors within the gene

stem: Why do the authors describe the recombination bias towards within-gene partners as self-reinforcing?
choices: Each event homogenizes the gene's sequences, raising the chance of the next one
Each event deletes competing donors from the genome
Each event raises the expression of the recombined synthetase
Each event shortens the gene, bringing domains closer together
answer: Each event homogenizes the gene's sequences, raising the chance of the next one
label: Results · self-reinforcing bias

stem: About how many different amino acids can non-ribosomal peptide synthetases theoretically incorporate, against which the authors contrast the alphabet actually accessible?
choices: Up to 22
Up to 300
Up to 60
Up to 1,000
answer: Up to 300
label: Discussion · theoretical alphabet

stem: Why do the authors call conventional protein evolution less constrained than NRP evolution?
choices: Point mutations are more frequent than recombinations
Proteins tolerate more substitutions before losing function
Any position is a few point mutations from any proteinogenic amino acid
Protein genes recombine with any partner regardless of similarity
answer: Any position is a few point mutations from any proteinogenic amino acid
label: Discussion · contrast with protein evolution

stem: What historical limit on studying NRP evolution do the authors highlight?
choices: Ancestral sequence reconstruction cannot resolve stereochemistry
Horizontal transfer erases the species signal in the gene tree
Side products are rarely recorded, so product spectra are incomplete
Each recombination overwrites the record of the sequence it replaces
answer: Each recombination overwrites the record of the sequence it replaces
label: Discussion · lost history
